title: Follow-on value and high-touch renewal (switching costs without traps)
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Whether to add follow-on offers, onboarding and success reviews that raise the value of staying, and whether the price can carry that labour.
applies_when: Customers stay but buy one thing
Agency or B2B retainers with renewal dates
exclusions: Activation or first-value problem unsolved (fix that first)
Lock-in that works by making leaving hard rather than staying valuable
required_inputs: Price per account and onboarding hours
Customer list with consent for account contact
evidence_requirements: existence of follow-on purchases (renewals, add-ons, repeat jobs)
what customers would lose by leaving (data, setup, training, relationships)
what was promised in the sale (goals, KPIs)
onboarding steps and owner/staff hours per client
usage or delivery signals per client
missing_data_behavior: No hours data: show the service-cost share as a question, not a number.
No renewal data: start with a manual review list.

decision_branches.if: Onboarding hours x rate is a large share of first-period price
decision_branches.then: Automated or group onboarding for low-price accounts; reserve live reviews for high-value ones.

decision_branches.if: Customers get repeat value and ask for adjacent work
decision_branches.then: Test one follow-on offer with existing customers (owner-approved message).

decision_branches.if: Leaving is hard but customers are unhappy
decision_branches.then: Not eligible: remove friction, fix value.

implementation_steps: Classify current switching costs: financial, procedural, relational
Measure attach rate and retention of attached customers
Review pricing for embedded customers with notice (PB-price-increase)
Kickoff: restate goals ('rediscovery') and confirm in writing.
Client does real work in the session.
dependencies: some paying customers; retention not broken
Sale notes captured at close: decision-maker, users, goals

cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: service or product able to deliver the follow-on
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: attach rate, retention by attached vs not

metrics: share of new clients onboarded within N days
share with a success review in the last quarter
guardrails: Cancelling stays as easy as buying.
Auto-renewal terms are an owner and legal decision, not a default.
Customers can always leave and take their data
Price changes to existing customers only with notice and owner approval
Renewal and cancellation terms clear and lawful where the business operates
Auto-renewal terms and notices follow local consumer/contract law (external)
Success reports show measured outcomes only, no invented results
Customer stories/testimonials only with client permission
alternatives_when_constrained: No customers yet: not applicable; use origination plays
One-off local consumer jobs: use retention-lifecycle rebooking/review flows instead of QBRs
No usage data: monthly 2-question check-in email
stop_conditions: Attach rate flat after 8 weeks: revise offer
If renewal rate falls, review onboarding completion and first-result timing first
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Dark patterns: hidden cancellation, blocked data export, surprise auto-renewal
Assuming lock-in justifies higher acquisition spend in a mature market
Group onboarding that leaves half-trained users

external_requirement.rule: proposed: never recommend raising switching costs by restricting exit (blocked export, hidden cancellation)
proposed: Auto-renewal clauses and reminder timing are flagged for the owner to check against local law; ClimbOS does not draft them as compliant.

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: when a business has follow-on purchases and attach rate under its own target, rank a follow-on offer play ahead of new acquisition plays of similar cost
proposed: Expansion or upsell suggestions are suppressed for clients with open delivery issues.

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: switching-cost claims do not raise affordable CAC unless observed retention supports the longer lifetime
proposed: Before recommending a high-touch onboarding, code computes onboarding labour cost per client and its share of first-period revenue; flag when it exceeds the owner's margin room.

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: Every onboarding plan ends with a booked back-check and a measurable first task.

reconciliation_note: Overlaps BRP-03 on add-ons; this playbook covers retention labour and renewal, BRP-03 covers package design.
